title: New Zealand AEWV Work Visa 2026 Guide
metaDescription: New Zealand Accredited Employer Work Visa 2026: job offer rules, NZ$35 median wage settings, 2 years experience, Job Check and residence pathways explained.
headline: New Zealand Accredited Employer Work Visa 2026

sections.title: What is the Accredited Employer Work Visa?
sections.content:
The Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV) is New Zealand's main temporary work visa. It is employer-led: you cannot apply on your own. You need a full-time job offer of at least 30 hours a week from an employer accredited by Immigration New Zealand, with an approved Job Check for your role.

The visa works in three stages: the employer gains accreditation, the employer passes a Job Check for the specific role, and then you apply. The maximum stay is up to five years for skill level 1 to 3 roles, and up to three years for skill level 4 and 5 roles.

sections.title: Pay rules in 2026
sections.content:
Since March 2025 there is no general median wage requirement for AEWV roles. Employers must pay at least the market rate for the job and never less than the legal minimum wage. The median wage still matters elsewhere: from 9 March 2026 it is NZ$35.00 an hour and applies to Green List pay floors, partner support and residence settings.

For a five-year stay in a skill level 1 to 3 role, one route is pay of at least NZ$52.50 an hour, which is 1.5 times the median wage. Always check the current Immigration New Zealand wage guidance before accepting an offer, because settings change frequently.

sections.title: Experience, English and the Job Check
sections.content:
For roles that require experience, you generally need at least two years of relevant work experience, reduced from three years in March 2025, or a relevant qualification at level 4 or higher on the New Zealand qualifications framework. English language requirements apply to skill level 3 to 5 roles.

The Job Check costs the employer NZ$735 and requires showing a genuine attempt to recruit New Zealanders first. For skill level 4 and 5 roles this includes engaging with Work and Income. Accredited employers are banned from charging recruitment fees to workers.

sections.title: Residence pathways and common mistakes
sections.content:
The AEWV itself is temporary, but it is the usual first step toward residence through the Green List or the Skilled Migrant Category. Roles on the Green List can lead to straight-to-residence or work-to-residence pathways, depending on the occupation and pay.

The most common mistakes are assuming the old median wage rule still sets AEWV pay, paying for a fake job offer, and changing jobs without a variation of conditions. Your visa is tied to your approved job, employer and location, so any change needs approval first.

faqs.q: Do I need a job offer for the New Zealand AEWV?
faqs.a: Yes, the AEWV is employer-led. You must have a full-time job offer of at least 30 hours a week from an accredited New Zealand employer whose Job Check has been approved before you can apply. Without that offer and approved Job Check, there is no AEWV application to make.

faqs.q: Is there still a median wage requirement for the AEWV?
faqs.a: No, the general median wage requirement was removed in March 2025. Employers must pay the market rate for the role and at least the legal minimum wage. The median wage of NZ$35.00 an hour from 9 March 2026 still applies to Green List pay floors, partner support and residence settings.

faqs.q: How long can I stay on an AEWV?
faqs.a: The maximum continuous stay is five years for skill level 1 to 3 roles, and three years for skill level 4 and 5 roles. A five-year stay in a skill level 1 to 3 role can also depend on meeting the higher pay threshold of NZ$52.50 an hour or being on the Green List.

faqs.q: How much experience do I need for the AEWV?
faqs.a: For roles that require experience, you generally need at least two years of relevant work experience, reduced from three years in March 2025. Alternatively, a relevant qualification at level 4 or higher on the New Zealand qualifications framework can satisfy the requirement for many roles.
